pinnedFiles.reason: Tick/Run/Once/Drain and the say()/record()/detail() console-output helpers already in use; the idle/waiting transition detection and the once-per-transition print are wired in here.
OrderState, Phase constants, Replay(), and IsActive() — the idle/waiting/running classification is built from these, not a new parallel state.
pendingWork/isClaimable/activeCount already compute 'running' and 'claimable'; the AC's 'none claimable' must reuse this exact test, not reimplement it.
Candidate.IsClaimable/IsReady and the Intake struct — what 'committed' (already loaded by the tick) holds going into the claimability check.

ItemKind/Inbox()/itemsFor() define the four waiting kinds (gate halt, commit proposal, PR proposal, parked) the AC names; the new count must agree with `loom factory inbox` without copying its filesystem/git calls (NFR: no extra pass per tick).
Event/Entry/Claim definitions (EventWaiting, EventProposed, EventParked, Claim.Finish) needed to classify phases from already-loaded state, with no new I/O.

finishCompleted's `Claim.Finish == "none"` rule — a completed order with finish:none ships immediately and is never a commit-proposal wait, so the waiting count must mirror this exactly or it will overcount.

Existing Tick-driven transition tests (e.g. TestAnOrphanedRunIsSettledFromItsState, TestTwoRunsStartAndTheThirdWaitsForASlot) are the style the new idle/waiting tests extend, asserting on the supervisor's output buffer.
testFactory/orderSpec/fakeLauncher/tick()/inbox() fixtures the new tests drive; Dependencies.Output currently has no buffer wired in newSupervisor, so this is also where that gets added.
The feature spec itself — exact wording of both printed lines, the four phases that count as waiting, and the retrying-order open question's resolved assumption (not waiting).
